thread.title: UPDATE: Nasdaq ends at record as tech leads stock-market rally

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Nasdaq ends at record as tech leads stock-market rally
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and William Watts, MarketWatch
Russell 2000 notches all-time high
U.S. stocks posted solid gains Monday, led by a rally in the technology and consumer discretionary sectors, as traders appeared to shrug off global trade tensions and focused on a favorable economic backdrop instead.
What did markets do?
The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record for the first time since March 12, rising 52.13 points, or 0.7%, to 7,606.46. It remained shy of its all-time intraday high of 7,637.27, hit on March 13.
The S&P 500 finished up 12.25 points, or 0.5%, to 2,746.87, with seven of its 11 sectors closing higher. Technology, consumer discretionary and consumer staples sectors led the gains, up about 1%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 178.48 points, or 0.7%, to 24,813.69.
The Russell 2000 also closed at a fresh all-time high, rising 5.39 points, or 0.3%, to 1,653.37.
What was driving the market?
Investors continued to cheer a round of solid U.S. jobs data released Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-gains-223000-new-jobs-in-may-unemployment-falls-to-18-year-of-38-2018-06-01), which showed the world's largest economy in better economic health than expected. That helped spur a move back into riskier assets such as stocks, after political upheaval in Italy earlier last week sparked a flight into havens such as bonds.
The optimism over the U.S. data also helped overshadow lingering concerns over global trade on Monday. A round of trade talks between the U.S. and China broke down over the weekend with no agreement, indicating a full-on trade war between the world's two largest economies could be imminent.
Read:China warns U.S.: Trade agreements are off if tariffs are imposed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-warns-us-trade-agreements-are-off-if-tariffs-are-imposed-2018-06-03)
Meanwhile, finance ministers from Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the U.K. issued a rare rebuke to the U.S (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/other-g-7-members-issue-rare-condemnation-of-us-tariffs-2018-06-03). at a G-7 meeting on Saturday, expressing their "unanimous concern and disappointment" about President Donald Trump's decision to place tariffs on metals imports from America's major allies.
Tariffs and trade are also likely to feature highly on the agenda when leaders of the G-7 nations -- including the U.S. -- hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday.
What are strategists saying?
"Retailers are doing well today because of the massive upgrade of Macy's by Evercore, which said that the worst is over for the sector," said Diane Jaffee, senior portfolio manager at TCW Group.
Read:The stock market's most-loved and most-hated equities have something in common (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-what-the-stock-markets-most-loved-and-most-hated-shares-have-in-common-2018-06-04)
"Latest economic reports indicate that consumers finally have confidence and extra income to spend on big-ticket items. Really low levels of unemployment and underemployment bode well for the retail sector and the market in general," Jaffee said.
"It is always a plus to have a tech behemoth like Apple touching all-time highs, since Apple makes up such a huge part of all three major indices," said Ken Berman, strategist at Gorilla Trades.
Shares of Apple Inc. closed at a record level of $191.83, bringing its market capitalization to $943 billion.
What was on the economic calendar?
U.S. factory orders (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-factory-orders-drop-08-in-april-2018-06-04)fell by 0.8% in April, driven by a decline in commercial aircraft.
There will be no Federal Reserve speeches as the central bank is in its so-called blackout period ahead of its June 12-13 meeting.
See:MarketWatch's economic calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Which stocks were in focus?
"Among the best performers on Wall Street were retail stocks, following a report by Evercore ISI, upgrading their entire retail portfolio, saying "Retailpocalypse is over." Shares of Target Corp. (TGT) rose 4.9% and Kohl's Corp. (KSS) rose 4.7%, while Macy's Inc.(M) rose 4.3% and Nordstrom Inc.(JWN) added 2.7%.
The SPDR S&P Retail ETF(XRT) rose 2.2% and is up 15% for the past 12 months.
Amazon.com Inc. stock (AMZN) rose 1.4% and closed at a record for the sixth session in a row, lifting its market capitalization above $800 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazons-market-cap-tops-800-billion-as-stock-surges-toward-6th-straight-record-2018-06-04) intraday, making it just the second U.S. company to top that level, behind Apple.
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) rose 0.8% as it kicked off the company's annual Worldwide Developers Conference. The gain is atypical given that the first day of the conference has often been a dud (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-how-apples-stock-traded-around-previous-wwdcs-2018-06-04) for Apple shares in the past, according to BTIG.
See:If Apple makes big news at WWDC, that would be big news (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/if-apple-makes-big-news-at-its-developers-conference-next-week-it-would-be-big-news-2018-06-01)
Facebook Inc.(FB) shares ended down 0.4%. The New York Times reported that the social media company made agreements with at least 60 makers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-made-deals-with-device-makers-that-gave-them-access-to-users-information-nyt-2018-06-04) of phones and other devices that gave them access to the personal information of users' friends without their consent. Facebook said it disagreed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-responds-to-nyt-story-on-data-sharing-says-we-disagree-with-issues-raised-2018-06-04) with the issues raised.
Shares of Microsoft Corp.(MSFT) rose 0.9% after the software giant said it had agreed to buy software-developer platform GitHub (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/microsoft-to-buy-github-for-75-billion-in-stock-2018-06-04) for $7.5 billion.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) rose 3.1% after surging 4.9% to end at a 10-month high Friday following a favorable analyst note (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amds-stock-surges-to-9-month-high-after-analyst-price-hike-cisco-adoption-2018-06-01).
Nektar Therapeutics Inc.(NKTR) shares plunged 42% after "underwhelming" results from clinical trials of its cancer drugs in combination with Bristol-Myers Squibb's cancer drug Opdivo. Shares of Bristol-Myers Squibb(BMY) fell 3.2%.
What did other markets do?
Asian stocks closed mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-rally-with-toyota-and-sony-boosting-nikkei-2018-06-03), as traders there got their first chance to react to the upbeat U.S. jobs data from Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 index ended 1.4% higher, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed 1.6%.
Europe closed higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-ma-cheer-replaces-political-fears-2018-06-04), with the Stoxx Europe 600 index gaining 0.3% to 388.11, its best finish in a week.
Crude oil prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-slip-as-investors-wait-for-opec-to-make-a-move-2018-06-04) settled 1.6% lower at $64.75 a barrel, while gold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-churns-below-1300-even-as-dollar-nicked-2018-06-04) settled 0.2% lower at $1,297.30 an ounce. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index fell 0.1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-slumps-as-us-trade-policies-rattle-investors-2018-06-04) to 94.077.
-Anora M. Gaudiano; 1711ET
